case_analysis.thread_summary: This thread is a long-running exchange (April 16 - June 13, 2025) between a customer ([COMPANY], contact [PERSON]) and Allion consultants ([PERSON], [PERSON]) covering the full SIG registration process for a board (79x50mm) built around a Bluetooth module, ending with notification that the Compliance Folder was shipped on CD-R after registration completion. Topics progress from pre-test scoping (RF/RF PHY exemption based on the module's antenna), through a quote question about Multi-Design vs Single Design reference fees tied to how the module is registered (Host Subsystem + Controller Subsystem QDIDs vs a single Component), through a Review Page Consistency Check warning resolved via TCW, to post-registration topics (Compliance Folder contents/retention and free registration of derivative products reusing the same module/stack).
all_questions_found: Does the customer's Bluetooth module require RF/RF PHY testing for SIG certification, given its datasheet describes its antenna configuration?
Is the Bluetooth module registered as a single SIG 'Component', or as separate Host Subsystem and Controller Subsystem QDIDs requiring a Multi-Design reference?
Why is the registration support cost higher this time compared to a previous quote?
What does a yellow warning on a Submission Requirement item (Consistency Check 'Invalid') on the Review Page mean, and can the registration still be submitted?
How long does SIG approval take after Submission, and how is the customer notified?
What is the Compliance Folder (received via CD-R) for, and how long must it be retained?
Can derivative products that reuse the same Bluetooth module and host stack be registered as additional models at no extra cost, and how is this done?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The module's datasheet documents either a built-in antenna or an antenna connector, which exempts the host product from RF/RF PHY testing. SIG's listing shows the module registered as a Host Subsystem QDID plus a separate Controller Subsystem QDID rather than as a single Component/End Product, requiring the host product to reference both QDIDs (Multi-Design reference). Since the July 1, 2024 rule change, this multi-QDID referencing triggers stricter Controller-Host consistency checks (e.g., ICS modifications), which is reflected in a higher support fee. During final Review Page checks, a Consistency Check 'Invalid' on a Submission Requirement item was identified as SIG-caused and covered by an existing TCW, allowing Submission to proceed; SIG approval followed within the typical 1-5 business day window. After registration, the Compliance Folder (operation manual Bluetooth section, block diagram, outline/dimension drawing, antenna data with radiation gain pattern) was shipped via tracked CD-R, with a 1-year post-sales retention requirement. Finally, derivative products reusing the same module and host stack can be added as free additional models via 'Manage Submitted Products' on My Page.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Each stage of the registration was resolved by checking specific reference documentation: the module datasheet (for RF/RF PHY exemption), SIG's QDID listing (for Component vs Host+Controller Subsystem combination and resulting Multi-Design fee), the Review Page's Consistency Check detail and applicable TCWs (for the Submission warning), and SIG's standard Compliance Folder and 'Manage Submitted Products' policies (for post-registration retention and derivative product handling).
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misreading the module's datasheet could lead to unnecessary RF/RF PHY testing or, conversely, a missed required test. Assuming a module is a single Component when it is actually a Host+Controller combination could lead to under-quoting and missing required Multi-Design verification work. Treating an SIG-caused, TCW-covered Consistency Check warning as a blocking error could stall Submission unnecessarily. Discarding the Compliance Folder before the 1-year post-sales retention period would leave the manufacturer unable to respond to an SIG audit. Treating a reusable derivative product as requiring a brand-new paid registration would incur unnecessary cost.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For module-based SIG registrations, always check the module datasheet for antenna configuration (RF/RF PHY exemption) and the SIG listing for whether the module is a single Component or a Host+Controller Subsystem combination (Multi-Design reference and fee implications, especially post-July 2024 consistency check rules). On the Review Page, a Consistency Check warning isn't automatically blocking - check whether it's SIG-caused and covered by a TCW before assuming submission must be delayed. After registration, retain the Compliance Folder for at least 1 year post-sales, and remember that derivative products sharing the same module and host stack can be registered for free via 'Manage Submitted Products'.
